candidate_relations.reason: The clinical and imaging findings (pancreatic swelling with peripheral rim, elevated amylase/lipase, association with ulcerative colitis, normal IgG4) are characteristic of autoimmune pancreatitis type 2, not chronic pancreatitis. Chronic pancreatitis implies a different pathological process with ductal dilation, calcifications, and fibrosis, which are not described here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Chronic pancreatitis is a different entity from autoimmune pancreatitis type 2; imaging here shows acute swelling with peripheral rim, not chronic fibrotic changes

candidate_relations.reason: Autoimmune pancreatitis type 1 is IgG4-related sclerosing disease with elevated serum IgG4, whereas this patient has a normal IgG4 (36 mg/dL), concurrent ulcerative colitis, and negative anti-GAD antibodies — all hallmarks of type 2 AIP (idiopathic duct-centric pancreatitis). Asserting type 1 conflicts with the subtype required by the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Type 1 AIP is IgG4-related and typically lacks IBD association; this case has normal IgG4 and concurrent ulcerative colitis, pointing to type 2 AIP
